chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from some of our companions, conveyed by Sa'd bin Turaif, from Al-Asbagh bin Nubata, from Al-Harith al-A'war al-Hamdani, who said: Ali said to his son, Hasan (peace be upon them both), among the questions he asked him: O my son, what is foolishness?
He said: Following the dishonourable and accompanying the seducers.

key_terms.الدَّنَاةِ: The lowly, dishonourable, or those of low status/character
key_terms.الْغَوَاةِ: The seducers, those who lead others astray, or deviants

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of foolishness according to Imam Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines foolishness (*al-safah*) not merely as lack of intellect, but as the moral failure of adhering to the lowly (*al-danah*) and associating with those who lead others astray (*al-ghawah*). This definition underscores the Shia emphasis on *wilayah* of companions, where spiritual integrity is maintained by avoiding the company of the morally weak and the misguided, a concept deeply rooted in the Imams' pedagogical approach to character formation.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by al-Himyari, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from some of our companions to whom Sa’d bin Turaif informed, from Asbagh bin Nubata, from Harith al-A’war al-Hamdani, that he said: Ali said to his son, Hasan, peace be upon them both, among his questions which he asked him of: O my son, what is foolishness?
He said: To follow the dishonourable and accompany the seducers.
